title: Console: scope reduction for lightweight dashboards and phased cost telemetry
creator: Sana Reddy
description:
Context: We need a narrow, production-safe slice of the Console insights surface that delivers meaningful value to early adopters while reducing engineering scope and risk for the March launch. This PRD addendum describes the scope cuts, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for: (1) lightweight dashboards (route-level top-line metrics), (2) deferred tracing (tracing links instead of full trace ingestion), and (3) an initial cost-breakdown widget with a single aggregation dimension.

Scope changes (summary):
- Dashboards: Ship a single consolidated \"Routes\" dashboard with three cards (QPS, p50 latency, error rate) for the first launch. Remove: per-model breakdowns, heatmaps, and custom tile creation.
- Tracing: Do not ingest application traces in the MVP. Instead: surface trace sample links to existing tracing systems (Datadog/Tempo) and include 'trace availability' indicator. Full distributed tracing ingestion will be deferred to a later cycle.
- Cost breakdown: Provide a per-route daily cost estimate (approximate) and a gross token breakdown (in/out) for the last 24h. Defer: per-customer cost attribution, token-level cost reconciliation, and cost forecasting.

Rationale: These cuts reduce backend work (no new trace ingest pipeline, limited aggregation ETL) while preserving the core developer experience: fast visibility into performance and rough cost signals. The team can iterate on richer snapshots once the runtime metrics and billing ingestion prove stable.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Pros: smaller QA surface, lower infra spend for telemetry storage, faster time-to-launch.
- Cons: less fine-grained observability for customers; customers requiring immediate per-token cost reconciliation will be asked to use exports. Mitigation: clear in-product messaging and export path.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) \"Routes\" dashboard appears for all customers in the alpha orgs and loads within 1.5s with sample data.
2) Three cards (QPS, p50 latency, error rate) show accurate last-24h aggregations and match runtime metrics within 5% margin for sampled workloads.
3) Trace links display when a request has an associated external trace (datadog:// or tempo:// link) and the UI shows a 'Trace link available' indicator when present.
4) Cost card shows per-route daily cost estimate and token counts for last 24h; numbers are derived from accepted lightweight aggregation pipeline and documented in the engineering notes.
5) Feature flag gating exists: Console telemetry surface must be toggleable per-organization before rollout.
6) Documentation: Shortstart doc and a wizard note explaining limitations (no per-token reconciliation, no per-customer attribution) published in Confluence and linked from the UI.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (week 1): enable for internal orgs + 3 pilot customers. Collect feedback and compare metrics vs runtime.
- Gradual (week 2): ramp to 20% orgs, monitor for errors and load.
- Full (week 3): enable by default for all new signups; existing orgs opt-in.

Metrics of success: adoption by pilot customers (qualitative), <2% error-rate increase on telemetry stack, and cost to store telemetry < 25% of projected full-feature cost for Q1.

QPS, p50 latency, and error rate cards match runtime metrics within 5% for sampled workloads
Trace link indicator displays and deep-links to external tracing when available
Per-route daily cost estimate and gross token counts display for last 24h
Feature flag exists to gate the telemetry surface per-organization
Shortstart docs published and linked from the UI explaining limitations

decisions: Defer full distributed trace ingestion; surface external trace links instead
Limit dashboards to a single consolidated Routes view with three top-line cards
Provide approximate per-route cost estimates only for MVP; defer precise reconciliation
